misconceptions.description: Adds the two denominators to get a 'common' denominator (1/4 and 1/6 -> 10).
Uses the larger denominator even though the smaller one doesn't divide into it (1/4 and 1/6 -> 6).
Adds the same amount to top and bottom instead of multiplying (1/4 = ?/12 -> 9).
Changes the denominator but leaves the numerator the same (1/4 = ?/12 -> 1).
Adds the numerators and adds the denominators (1/2 + 1/3 -> 2/5).
Subtracts the numerators and subtracts the denominators (3/4 - 1/2 -> 2/2).
Finds a common denominator but doesn't rewrite the numerators (1/2 + 1/3 -> 2/6).
Multiplies only the top, not the bottom (2/5 by 3 -> 6/5).
Adds the number to the top and bottom instead of multiplying (2/5 by 3 -> 5/8).
Gives the starting fraction back instead of the scaled one (2/5 by 3 -> 2/5).
Adds the same amount to top and bottom to fill the box (3/4 = ?/12 -> 11).
Divides only the top when simplifying (6/8 -> 3/8).
Compares shaded parts to unshaded parts instead of to all the parts (3 shaded, 2 not -> 3/2).
Names the unshaded part instead of the shaded part (3 of 5 shaded -> 2/5).
Counts the tick marks instead of the spaces between 0 and 1 (fourths -> fifths).
Treats the whole line as one whole when it goes past 1 (5/4 on a 0-2 line -> 5/8).
Writes the division upside down (3 / 4 -> 4/3).
Subtracts instead of dividing to turn a fraction into a whole number (12/4 -> 8).
Compares only the tops (2/7 vs 1/2 -> 2/7 is bigger because 2 > 1).
Thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction (3/8 > 3/5).
Thinks fractions missing the same number of pieces are equal (3/4 = 5/6).
Keeps the denominator when multiplying, as if adding (2/5 × 3/5 -> 6/5).
Multiplies across diagonally (2/3 × 4/5 -> 10/12).
Adds the fractions instead of multiplying.
Multiplies both the top and the bottom by the whole number (3 × 2/7 -> 6/21).
Multiplies the bottom by the whole number instead of the top (3 × 2/7 -> 2/21).
For a fraction of an amount, divides by the bottom but doesn't multiply by the top (2/3 of 12 -> 4).
